FAILURE HANDLING & RECOVERY\n\n**Failure Context Accumulation:**\nWhen verification fails, `.ralph/last_failure.txt` is created with:\n```\n=== Attempt 1 failed for TASK-001 ===\n[verification output - last 50 lines]\n---\n=== Attempt 2 failed for TASK-001 ===\n[new verification output]\n---\n```\n\nThis cumulative context helps Claude identify patterns:\n- \"Same error 3 times?\" → Structural issue (missing migration, wrong approach)\n- \"Different errors?\" → Implementation bugs to fix\n\n**Structural Error Detection:**\nCode detects errors that can't be fixed by retrying:\n- \"column does not exist\" → Suggest DB reset (schema mismatch)\n- \"pending migration\" → Suggest running migrations\n- \"connection refused\" → Suggest starting services\n- \"relation X does not exist\" → Database schema issue\n\nThese are flagged with actionable suggestions instead of infinite retries.\n\n**Circuit Breakers:**\n1. **Max retries per story**: 15 attempts (configurable via `maxStoryRetries`)\n2. **Max consecutive timeouts**: 5 timeouts → skip story (too large)\n3. **API crash limit**: 5 crashes → wait 60s before retrying\n\nWhen hit, story is marked `skipped: true` with reason, and loop continues.\n\n---\n\n### 12. If any fail → save failure context, retry (max 5 retries per story, then stop loop)\n\n**Key functions:**\n- `verify_prd_criteria()` in `ralph/verify/tests.sh:280-333` — iterates testSteps, expands config placeholders, runs each via `safe_exec()`\n- `safe_exec()` in `ralph/utils.sh:474-486` — validates then runs `bash -c \"$cmd\"` with NO timeout\n- `run_with_timeout()` in `ralph/utils.sh:310-322` — cross-platform timeout wrapper (uses `timeout`/`gtimeout`/fallback)\n- `_detect_structural_errors()` in `ralph/code-check.sh:243-326` — already detects DB schema issues, pending migrations, and \"connection refused\" patterns\n- `save_failure_context()` in `ralph/code-check.sh:191-235` — accumulates errors across retries\n- `log_progress()` in `ralph/utils.sh:105-124` — writes to .ralph/progress.txt\n\n**Constants** in `ralph/utils.sh`:\n- `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600` (Claude session)\n- `CURL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=10` \n- `BROWSER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=60`\n- No constant for testStep timeout\n\n**Circuit breaker for Claude session**: consecutive_timeouts ≥ 5 → skip story. But no circuit breaker for verification steps.\n\n**Progress log**: Ralph logs \"COMPLETED TASK-XXX\" to .ralph/progress.txt but NEVER reads it to determine if work is done. Only reads prd.json `passes: true`.\n\n## Three Gaps to Fix\n\n### Gap 1: No timeout on individual testSteps\n`verify_prd_criteria()` calls `safe_exec()` which is just `bash -c \"$cmd\"` with no timeout. If a Playwright test hangs waiting for a browser, or a curl hits a slow server, the step runs forever. The 600s Claude session timeout doesn't apply here because verification runs AFTER Claude returns.\n\n**Proposed fix:** Add a `TEST_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` constant (default 120s) and wrap `safe_exec` calls in `verify_prd_criteria()` with `run_with_timeout`.\n\n### Gap 2: No infrastructure vs code failure distinction at verification time\n`_detect_structural_errors()` already detects \"connection refused\" and DB issues, but it only appends suggestions to the failure context — it doesn't change the retry behavior. Ralph still burns all 5 retries on infrastructure failures.\n\n**Proposed fix:** When structural errors are detected (connection refused, DB schema, pending migrations), count them as \"infra failures\" rather than code failures. After 2 consecutive infra failures on the same category, skip the story with a clear message instead of burning all 5 retries. Use the existing `skipped_stories` mechanism (like timeout skipping).\n\n### Gap 3: No progress awareness\nRalph logs \"COMPLETED TASK-007, all tests passing\" to progress.txt, but when it restarts, it only checks `prd.json` `passes: true`. If the hook (now removed) or a git commit failure prevented `passes: true` from being written, Ralph re-does work it already completed.\n\n**Proposed fix:** At story selection time, check if progress.txt contains \"COMPLETED $story_id\". If it does but `passes: false` in prd.json, auto-heal: set `passes: true` and skip to the next story. Log a warning that this was auto-healed.\n\n## Design Constraints\n- Bash 3.2 compatible (no associative arrays)\n- Follow existing patterns: use constants from utils.sh, use `get_config` for configurables\n- Keep changes minimal — don't restructure the entire loop\n- All changes should be backward-compatible (existing configs still work)\n\nPlease design the implementation with specific file changes, function modifications, and new constants needed.","agentId":"a8f1ea5"},"toolUseID":"agent_msg_01HNt7ad2bBvpz4Fbjqis5Ss","parentToolUseID":"toolu_01U5jtAuxX9hVJyMWsAssgp5","uuid":"619e22ce-dbcd-4fef-be02-dd618c947693","timestamp":"2026-02-04T03:36:51.336Z"}

Every Ralph session includes this context.\n\n### /styleguide - UI Consistency\n\nGenerate a component reference for consistent frontend design:\n\n```bash\n/styleguide\n```\n\nCreates an HTML styleguide at `docs/styleguide.html` showing your colors, typography, and component patterns. Frontend stories reference this automatically.\n\n### /sign - Teach Patterns\n\nWhen Ralph makes the same mistake repeatedly, teach it:\n\n```bash\n# Via CLI\nnpx agentic-loop sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n\n# Via Claude session\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nSigns are saved to `.ralph/signs.json` and injected into every prompt.\n\n### config.json - Tune Your Setup\n\nProject-specific configuration in `.ralph/config.json`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"urls\": {\n    \"frontend\": \"http://localhost:3000\",\n    \"backend\": \"http://localhost:8000\"\n  },\n  \"checks\": {\n    \"lint\": true,\n    \"test\": true\n  },\n  \"maxSessionSeconds\": 600,\n  \"maxStoryRetries\": 8\n}\n```\n\nSee [Configuration Reference](RALPH.md#configuration-reference) for all options.\n\n### /prd-check - Custom Preflight Checks\n\nRalph validates every PRD before the loop starts, catching issues early (missing test steps, vague requirements) instead of failing mid-execution. You can extend this with your own checks.\n\n#### Running PRD Validation\n\n```bash\n# Full validation with auto-fix\nralph prd-check\n\n# Dry run — show issues without fixing\nralph prd-check --dry-run\n\n# Check a specific PRD file\nralph prd-check .ralph/prd.json\n```\n\n#### Adding Custom Checks\n\nCustom checks live in `.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project. Ask Claude to create them for you:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description field\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling test steps\n```\n\nClaude knows the check script interface (receives story JSON on stdin, outputs issues to stdout) and will create the script in the right location with the right permissions.\n\n#### Enabling/Disabling Individual Checks\n\nToggle specific checks in `.ralph/config.json` using the script filename (without extension) as the key:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"checks\": {\n    \"custom\": {\n      \"check-description\": true,\n      \"check-complexity\": false\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nChecks default to enabled. Set to `false` to skip a check.\n\n#### How Custom Checks Differ from Built-in Checks\n\n| | Built-in checks | Custom checks |\n|---|---|---|\n| Auto-fix by Claude | Yes | No — reported for manual review |\n| Timeout | None | 30 seconds per script |\n| Scope | Project-level | Project-level |\n| Configuration | `.checks.*` | `.checks.custom.<name>` |\n\n---\n\n## Built-in Guardrails\n\n### On-Demand Quality Checks\n\n| Command | What It Does |\n|---------|--------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scan for AI coding patterns (console.logs, TODOs, dead code) |\n| `/review` | Code review for issues, improvements, best practices |\n\n### Pre-commit Hooks\n\nAutomatically installed during setup. Block commits that contain:\n\n- Secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens)\n- Hardcoded URLs (localhost, 127.0.0.1)\n- Debug statements (console.log, debugger, print)\n- TODO/FIXME comments\n\n```bash\n# Install/reinstall hooks\nnpx agentic-loop setup\n```\n\nSee [Hooks Reference](HOOKS.md) for configuration.\n\n### Claude Code Hooks\n\nReal-time warnings while Claude is coding:\n\n- Warns when creating files that might contain secrets\n- Warns on hardcoded URLs in code\n- Warns on debug statements\n\nConfigured in `.claude/settings.json`. See [Hooks Reference](HOOKS.md).\n\n### Test File Enforcement\n\nCode check fails if new code lacks corresponding tests:\n\n```\nERROR: New file src/utils/auth.ts has no test file\nExpected: src/utils/auth.test.ts or tests/utils/auth.test.ts\n```\n\nDisable in config:\n```json\n{\n  \"checks\": {\n    \"requireTests\": false\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [Hooks Reference](HOOKS.md) - Detailed hook configuration\n- [How Ralph Works](RALPH.md) - Full architecture\n- [Cheatsheet](CHEATSHEET.md) - All commands at a glance\n"},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0dcbc8d2-b057-4763-ba6d-5b1897d061a2"}

These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\nEverything here is done by talking to Claude — no config files to edit by hand.\n\n---\n\n## Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n## Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n## Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n---\n\n## Check Your PRD Before Running\n\nBefore Ralph starts building, it validates your PRD to catch problems early — missing test steps, vague requirements, stories that would fail immediately. You can run this yourself anytime:\n\n```\nralph prd-check\n```\n\nIf it finds issues, Claude will try to fix them automatically. You can also preview what it would flag without changing anything:\n\n```\nralph prd-check --dry-run\n```\n\n### Add Your Own Preflight Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quality Checks You Can Run Anytime\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## What Ralph Catches Automatically\n\nRalph has built-in safety checks that run without you doing anything. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\n---\n\n## What Happens Automatically\n\nThese features are set up and run for you — no manual steps needed.\n\n### Setup (`npx agentic-loop setup`)\n\nWhen you run setup, Ralph automatically:\n\n- **Detects your project type** (Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, fullstack) and creates `.ralph/config.json` with sensible defaults — test commands, URLs, directories\n- **Installs pre-commit hooks** that block secrets, hardcoded URLs, debug statements, and TODO/FIXME comments from being committed\n- **Installs Claude Code hooks** that warn in real-time while Claude is coding — catching secrets, hardcoded URLs, and debug statements before they're even saved\n- **Installs timeout utilities** on macOS (via `brew install coreutils`) so session time limits are enforced reliably\n\n### During the Loop (`npx agentic-loop run`)\n\nEach time Ralph starts or processes a story, it automatically:\n\n- **Runs preflight checks** — verifies API/frontend connectivity, Docker services, database migrations, and timeout utilities before starting\n- **Validates your PRD** — checks for missing test steps, vague requirements, and structural issues. If it finds problems, Claude auto-fixes them\n- **Verifies code after Claude writes it** — runs a 5-step pipeline: lint, unit tests, PRD test steps, API smoke test, frontend smoke test\n- **Learns from retries** — when a story fails then passes after retries, Ralph extracts what went wrong as a \"sign\" and remembers it for future stories (when `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config)\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Customize\n\nThese are things you run yourself to teach Ralph your preferences.\n\n### Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n### Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n### Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n> **Also automatic:** When `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config, Ralph extracts signs on its own from stories that fail then succeed after retries. You can review auto-extracted signs in `.ralph/signs.json`.\n\n---\n\n### Add Your Own PRD Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. See [Configuration Reference](RALPH.md#configuration-reference) for everything that's configurable.\n\n---\n\n### On-Demand Quality Checks\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Feature | When it runs | Automatic or manual? |\n|---------|-------------|---------------------|\n| Project detection + config | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic |\n| Pre-commit hooks | Every `git commit` | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Claude Code hooks | While Claude edits files | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Timeout utility install | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic (macOS with Homebrew) |\n| Preflight checks | Start of `npx agentic-loop run` | Automatic |\n| PRD validation + auto-fix | Start of loop | Automatic |\n| Code verification (5-step) | After Claude writes each story | Automatic |\n| Sign auto-promotion | After story retry succeeds | Automatic (if enabled) |\n| `/my-dna` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/styleguide` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/sign` | When you run it | Manual |\n| Custom PRD checks | When you create them | Manual (then runs automatically) |\n| `/vibe-check` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/review` | When you run it | Manual |\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [Cheatsheet](CHEATSHEET.md) — All commands at a glance\n- [How Ralph Works](RALPH.md) — Full architecture\n- [Hooks Reference](HOOKS.md) — Details on the safety checks\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":2,"oldLines":12,"newStart":2,"newLines":38,"lines":[" "," Ralph works out of the box, but every project is different. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\n---\n\n## What Happens Automatically\n\nThese features are set up and run for you — no manual steps needed.\n\n### Setup (`npx agentic-loop setup`)\n\nWhen you run setup, Ralph automatically:\n\n- **Detects your project type** (Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, fullstack) and creates `.ralph/config.json` with sensible defaults — test commands, URLs, directories\n- **Installs pre-commit hooks** that block secrets, hardcoded URLs, debug statements, and TODO/FIXME comments from being committed\n- **Installs Claude Code hooks** that warn in real-time while Claude is coding — catching secrets, hardcoded URLs, and debug statements before they're even saved\n- **Installs timeout utilities** on macOS (via `brew install coreutils`) so session time limits are enforced reliably\n\n### During the Loop (`npx agentic-loop run`)\n\nEach time Ralph starts or processes a story, it automatically:\n\n- **Runs preflight checks** — verifies API/frontend connectivity, Docker services, database migrations, and timeout utilities before starting\n- **Validates your PRD** — checks for missing test steps, vague requirements, and structural issues. If it finds problems, Claude auto-fixes them\n- **Verifies code after Claude writes it** — runs a 5-step pipeline: lint, unit tests, PRD test steps, API smoke test, frontend smoke test\n- **Learns from retries** — when a story fails then passes after retries, Ralph extracts what went wrong as a \"sign\" and remembers it for future stories (when `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config)\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Customize\n\nThese are things you run yourself to teach Ralph your preferences.\n\n### Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n### Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n### Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n> **Also automatic:** When `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config, Ralph extracts signs on its own from stories that fail then succeed after retries. You can review auto-extracted signs in `.ralph/signs.json`.\n\n---\n\n### Add Your Own PRD Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. See [Configuration Reference](RALPH.md#configuration-reference) for everything that's configurable.\n\n---\n\n### On-Demand Quality Checks\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Feature | When it runs | Automatic or manual? |\n|---------|-------------|---------------------|\n| Project detection + config | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic |\n| Pre-commit hooks | Every `git commit` | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Claude Code hooks | While Claude edits files | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Timeout utility install | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic (macOS with Homebrew) |\n| Preflight checks | Start of `npx agentic-loop run` | Automatic |\n| PRD validation + auto-fix | Start of loop | Automatic |\n| Code verification (5-step) | After Claude writes each story | Automatic |\n| Sign auto-promotion | After story retry succeeds | Automatic (if enabled) |\n| `/my-dna` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/styleguide` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/sign` | When you run it | Manual |\n| Custom PRD checks | When you create them | Manual (then runs automatically) |\n| `/vibe-check` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/review` | When you run it | Manual |\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [Cheatsheet](CHEATSHEET.md) — All commands at a glance\n- [How Ralph Works](RALPH.md) — Full architecture\n- [Hooks Reference](HOOKS.md) — Details on the safety checks\n"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2681,"cache_read_input_tokens":55083,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2681},"output_tokens":24,"service_tier":"standard"}},"requestId":"req_011CXnMgJUAuGT4JWE9D6A1q","type":"assistant","uuid":"7138965b-4c88-4c67-8196-e28e4ad53396","timestamp":"2026-02-04T03:58:02.156Z"}

This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\n---\n\n## What Happens Automatically\n\nThese features are set up and run for you — no manual steps needed.\n\n### Setup (`npx agentic-loop setup`)\n\nWhen you run setup, Ralph automatically:\n\n- **Detects your project type** (Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, fullstack) and creates `.ralph/config.json` with sensible defaults — test commands, URLs, directories\n- **Installs pre-commit hooks** that block secrets, hardcoded URLs, debug statements, and TODO/FIXME comments from being committed\n- **Installs Claude Code hooks** that warn in real-time while Claude is coding — catching secrets, hardcoded URLs, and debug statements before they're even saved\n- **Installs timeout utilities** on macOS (via `brew install coreutils`) so session time limits are enforced reliably\n\n### During the Loop (`npx agentic-loop run`)\n\nEach time Ralph starts or processes a story, it automatically:\n\n- **Runs preflight checks** — verifies API/frontend connectivity, Docker services, database migrations, and timeout utilities before starting\n- **Validates your PRD** — checks for missing test steps, vague requirements, and structural issues. If it finds problems, Claude auto-fixes them\n- **Verifies code after Claude writes it** — runs a 5-step pipeline: lint, unit tests, PRD test steps, API smoke test, frontend smoke test\n- **Learns from retries** — when a story fails then passes after retries, Ralph extracts what went wrong as a \"sign\" and remembers it for future stories (when `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config)\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Customize\n\nThese are things you run yourself to teach Ralph your preferences.\n\n### Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n### Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n### Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n> **Also automatic:** When `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config, Ralph extracts signs on its own from stories that fail then succeed after retries. You can review auto-extracted signs in `.ralph/signs.json`.\n\n---\n\n### Add Your Own PRD Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\nEverything here is done by talking to Claude — no config files to edit by hand.\n\n---\n\n## Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n## Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n## Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n---\n\n## Check Your PRD Before Running\n\nBefore Ralph starts building, it validates your PRD to catch problems early — missing test steps, vague requirements, stories that would fail immediately. You can run this yourself anytime:\n\n```\nralph prd-check\n```\n\nIf it finds issues, Claude will try to fix them automatically. You can also preview what it would flag without changing anything:\n\n```\nralph prd-check --dry-run\n```\n\n### Add Your Own Preflight Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quality Checks You Can Run Anytime\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## What Ralph Catches Automatically\n\nRalph has built-in safety checks that run without you doing anything. These are already set up when you install agentic-loop.\n\n**Before code gets committed**, Ralph blocks:\n- Secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens)\n- Hardcoded URLs (localhost, 127.0.0.1)\n- Debug statements left in the code\n- TODO/FIXME comments\n\n**While Claude is writing code**, it gets warnings about:\n- Files that might contain secrets\n- Hardcoded URLs\n- Debug statements\n\n**After code is written**, Ralph checks that new code has matching test files. If you see something like:\n\n```\nERROR: New file src/utils/auth.ts has no test file\n```\n\nThat means Ralph wants a test alongside the new code. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\n---\n\n## What Happens Automatically\n\nThese features are set up and run for you — no manual steps needed.\n\n### Setup (`npx agentic-loop setup`)\n\nWhen you run setup, Ralph automatically:\n\n- **Detects your project type** (Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, fullstack) and creates `.ralph/config.json` with sensible defaults — test commands, URLs, directories\n- **Installs pre-commit hooks** that block secrets, hardcoded URLs, debug statements, and TODO/FIXME comments from being committed\n- **Installs Claude Code hooks** that warn in real-time while Claude is coding — catching secrets, hardcoded URLs, and debug statements before they're even saved\n- **Installs timeout utilities** on macOS (via `brew install coreutils`) so session time limits are enforced reliably\n\n### During the Loop (`npx agentic-loop run`)\n\nEach time Ralph starts or processes a story, it automatically:\n\n- **Runs preflight checks** — verifies API/frontend connectivity, Docker services, database migrations, and timeout utilities before starting\n- **Validates your PRD** — checks for missing test steps, vague requirements, and structural issues. If it finds problems, Claude auto-fixes them\n- **Verifies code after Claude writes it** — runs a 5-step pipeline: lint, unit tests, PRD test steps, API smoke test, frontend smoke test\n- **Learns from retries** — when a story fails then passes after retries, Ralph extracts what went wrong as a \"sign\" and remembers it for future stories (when `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config)\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Customize\n\nThese are things you run yourself to teach Ralph your preferences.\n\n### Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\n---\n\n## What Happens Automatically\n\nThese features are set up and run for you — no manual steps needed.\n\n### Setup (`npx agentic-loop setup`)\n\nWhen you run setup, Ralph automatically:\n\n- **Detects your project type** (Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, fullstack) and creates `.ralph/config.json` with sensible defaults — test commands, URLs, directories\n- **Installs pre-commit hooks** that block secrets, hardcoded URLs, debug statements, and TODO/FIXME comments from being committed\n- **Installs Claude Code hooks** that warn in real-time while Claude is coding — catching secrets, hardcoded URLs, and debug statements before they're even saved\n- **Installs timeout utilities** on macOS (via `brew install coreutils`) so session time limits are enforced reliably\n\n### During the Loop (`npx agentic-loop run`)\n\nEach time Ralph starts or processes a story, it automatically:\n\n- **Runs preflight checks** — verifies API/frontend connectivity, Docker services, database migrations, and timeout utilities before starting\n- **Validates your PRD** — checks for missing test steps, vague requirements, and structural issues. If it finds problems, Claude auto-fixes them\n- **Verifies code after Claude writes it** — runs a 5-step pipeline: lint, unit tests, PRD test steps, API smoke test, frontend smoke test\n- **Learns from retries** — when a story fails then passes after retries, Ralph extracts what went wrong as a \"sign\" and remembers it for future stories (when `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config)\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Customize\n\nThese are things you run yourself to teach Ralph your preferences.\n\n### Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n### Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n### Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n> **Also automatic:** When `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config, Ralph extracts signs on its own from stories that fail then succeed after retries. You can review auto-extracted signs in `.ralph/signs.json`.\n\n---\n\n### Add Your Own PRD Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. See [Configuration Reference](RALPH.md#configuration-reference) for everything that's configurable.\n\n---\n\n### On-Demand Quality Checks\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Feature | When it runs | Automatic or manual? |\n|---------|-------------|---------------------|\n| Project detection + config | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic |\n| Pre-commit hooks | Every `git commit` | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Claude Code hooks | While Claude edits files | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Timeout utility install | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic (macOS with Homebrew) |\n| Preflight checks | Start of `npx agentic-loop run` | Automatic |\n| PRD validation + auto-fix | Start of loop | Automatic |\n| Code verification (5-step) | After Claude writes each story | Automatic |\n| Sign auto-promotion | After story retry succeeds | Automatic (if enabled) |\n| `/my-dna` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/styleguide` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/sign` | When you run it | Manual |\n| Custom PRD checks | When you create them | Manual (then runs automatically) |\n| `/vibe-check` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/review` | When you run it | Manual |\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [Cheatsheet](CHEATSHEET.md) — All commands at a glance\n- [How Ralph Works](RALPH.md) — Full architecture\n- [Hooks Reference](HOOKS.md) — Details on the safety checks\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":2,"oldLines":12,"newStart":2,"newLines":38,"lines":[" "," Ralph works out of the box, but every project is different. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n### Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n### Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n> **Also automatic:** When `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config, Ralph extracts signs on its own from stories that fail then succeed after retries. You can review auto-extracted signs in `.ralph/signs.json`.\n\n---\n\n### Add Your Own PRD Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. You can run this yourself anytime:\n\n```\nralph prd-check\n```\n\nIf it finds issues, Claude will try to fix them automatically. You can also preview what it would flag without changing anything:\n\n```\nralph prd-check --dry-run\n```\n\n### Add Your Own Preflight Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quality Checks You Can Run Anytime\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## What Ralph Catches Automatically\n\nRalph has built-in safety checks that run without you doing anything. These are already set up when you install agentic-loop.\n\n**Before code gets committed**, Ralph blocks:\n- Secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens)\n- Hardcoded URLs (localhost, 127.0.0.1)\n- Debug statements left in the code\n- TODO/FIXME comments\n\n**While Claude is writing code**, it gets warnings about:\n- Files that might contain secrets\n- Hardcoded URLs\n- Debug statements\n\n**After code is written**, Ralph checks that new code has matching test files. If you see something like:\n\n```\nERROR: New file src/utils/auth.ts has no test file\n```\n\nThat means Ralph wants a test alongside the new code. If your project doesn't use that pattern, tell Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the test file requirement in Ralph config\n```\n\n---\n\n## Tune Your Setup\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\n---\n\n## What Happens Automatically\n\nThese features are set up and run for you — no manual steps needed.\n\n### Setup (`npx agentic-loop setup`)\n\nWhen you run setup, Ralph automatically:\n\n- **Detects your project type** (Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, fullstack) and creates `.ralph/config.json` with sensible defaults — test commands, URLs, directories\n- **Installs pre-commit hooks** that block secrets, hardcoded URLs, debug statements, and TODO/FIXME comments from being committed\n- **Installs Claude Code hooks** that warn in real-time while Claude is coding — catching secrets, hardcoded URLs, and debug statements before they're even saved\n- **Installs timeout utilities** on macOS (via `brew install coreutils`) so session time limits are enforced reliably\n\n### During the Loop (`npx agentic-loop run`)\n\nEach time Ralph starts or processes a story, it automatically:\n\n- **Runs preflight checks** — verifies API/frontend connectivity, Docker services, database migrations, and timeout utilities before starting\n- **Validates your PRD** — checks for missing test steps, vague requirements, and structural issues. If it finds problems, Claude auto-fixes them\n- **Verifies code after Claude writes it** — runs a 5-step pipeline: lint, unit tests, PRD test steps, API smoke test, frontend smoke test\n- **Learns from retries** — when a story fails then passes after retries, Ralph extracts what went wrong as a \"sign\" and remembers it for future stories (when `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config)\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Customize\n\nThese are things you run yourself to teach Ralph your preferences.\n\n### Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n### Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n### Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n> **Also automatic:** When `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config, Ralph extracts signs on its own from stories that fail then succeed after retries. You can review auto-extracted signs in `.ralph/signs.json`.\n\n---\n\n### Add Your Own PRD Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. See [Configuration Reference](RALPH.md#configuration-reference) for everything that's configurable.\n\n---\n\n### On-Demand Quality Checks\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Feature | When it runs | Automatic or manual? This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\nEverything here is done by talking to Claude — no config files to edit by hand.\n\n---\n\n## Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\n---\n\n## What Happens Automatically\n\nThese features are set up and run for you — no manual steps needed.\n\n### Setup (`npx agentic-loop setup`)\n\nWhen you run setup, Ralph automatically:\n\n- **Detects your project type** (Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, fullstack) and creates `.ralph/config.json` with sensible defaults — test commands, URLs, directories\n- **Installs pre-commit hooks** that block secrets, hardcoded URLs, debug statements, and TODO/FIXME comments from being committed\n- **Installs Claude Code hooks** that warn in real-time while Claude is coding — catching secrets, hardcoded URLs, and debug statements before they're even saved\n- **Installs timeout utilities** on macOS (via `brew install coreutils`) so session time limits are enforced reliably\n\n### During the Loop (`npx agentic-loop run`)\n\nEach time Ralph starts or processes a story, it automatically:\n\n- **Runs preflight checks** — verifies API/frontend connectivity, Docker services, database migrations, and timeout utilities before starting\n- **Validates your PRD** — checks for missing test steps, vague requirements, and structural issues. If it finds problems, Claude auto-fixes them\n- **Verifies code after Claude writes it** — runs a 5-step pipeline: lint, unit tests, PRD test steps, API smoke test, frontend smoke test\n- **Learns from retries** — when a story fails then passes after retries, Ralph extracts what went wrong as a \"sign\" and remembers it for future stories (when `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config)\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Customize\n\nThese are things you run yourself to teach Ralph your preferences.\n\n### Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n### Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n### Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n> **Also automatic:** When `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config, Ralph extracts signs on its own from stories that fail then succeed after retries. You can review auto-extracted signs in `.ralph/signs.json`.\n\n---\n\n### Add Your Own PRD Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. See [Configuration Reference](RALPH.md#configuration-reference) for everything that's configurable.\n\n---\n\n### On-Demand Quality Checks\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Feature | When it runs | Automatic or manual? |\n|---------|-------------|---------------------|\n| Project detection + config | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic |\n| Pre-commit hooks | Every `git commit` | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Claude Code hooks | While Claude edits files | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Timeout utility install | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic (macOS with Homebrew) |\n| Preflight checks | Start of `npx agentic-loop run` | Automatic |\n| PRD validation + auto-fix | Start of loop | Automatic |\n| Code verification (5-step) | After Claude writes each story | Automatic |\n| Sign auto-promotion | After story retry succeeds | Automatic (if enabled) |\n| `/my-dna` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/styleguide` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/sign` | When you run it | Manual |\n| Custom PRD checks | When you create them | Manual (then runs automatically) |\n| `/vibe-check` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/review` | When you run it | Manual |\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [Cheatsheet](CHEATSHEET.md) — All commands at a glance\n- [How Ralph Works](RALPH.md) — Full architecture\n- [Hooks Reference](HOOKS.md) — Details on the safety checks\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":2,"oldLines":12,"newStart":2,"newLines":38,"lines":[" "," Ralph works out of the box, but every project is different. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\nEverything here is done by talking to Claude — no config files to edit by hand.\n\n---\n\n## Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n## Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n## Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n---\n\n## Check Your PRD Before Running\n\nBefore Ralph starts building, it validates your PRD to catch problems early — missing test steps, vague requirements, stories that would fail immediately. You can run this yourself anytime:\n\n```\nralph prd-check\n```\n\nIf it finds issues, Claude will try to fix them automatically. You can also preview what it would flag without changing anything:\n\n```\nralph prd-check --dry-run\n```\n\n### Add Your Own Preflight Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quality Checks You Can Run Anytime\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## What Ralph Catches Automatically\n\nRalph has built-in safety checks that run without you doing anything. These are already set up when you install agentic-loop.\n\n**Before code gets committed**, Ralph blocks:\n- Secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens)\n- Hardcoded URLs (localhost, 127.0.0.1)\n- Debug statements left in the code\n- TODO/FIXME comments\n\n**While Claude is writing code**, it gets warnings about:\n- Files that might contain secrets\n- Hardcoded URLs\n- Debug statements\n\n**After code is written**, Ralph checks that new code has matching test files. If you see something like:\n\n```\nERROR: New file src/utils/auth.ts has no test file\n```\n\nThat means Ralph wants a test alongside the new code. If your project doesn't use that pattern, tell Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the test file requirement in Ralph config\n```\n\n---\n\n## Tune Your Setup\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. See [Configuration Reference](RALPH.md#configuration-reference) for everything that's configurable.\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [Cheatsheet](CHEATSHEET.md) — All commands at a glance\n- [How Ralph Works](RALPH.md) — Full architecture\n- [Hooks Reference](HOOKS.md) — Details on the safety checks\n"},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"7138965b-4c88-4c67-8196-e28e4ad53396"}

This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\n---\n\n## What Happens Automatically\n\nThese features are set up and run for you — no manual steps needed.\n\n### Setup (`npx agentic-loop setup`)\n\nWhen you run setup, Ralph automatically:\n\n- **Detects your project type** (Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, fullstack) and creates `.ralph/config.json` with sensible defaults — test commands, URLs, directories\n- **Installs pre-commit hooks** that block secrets, hardcoded URLs, debug statements, and TODO/FIXME comments from being committed\n- **Installs Claude Code hooks** that warn in real-time while Claude is coding — catching secrets, hardcoded URLs, and debug statements before they're even saved\n- **Installs timeout utilities** on macOS (via `brew install coreutils`) so session time limits are enforced reliably\n\n### During the Loop (`npx agentic-loop run`)\n\nEach time Ralph starts or processes a story, it automatically:\n\n- **Runs preflight checks** — verifies API/frontend connectivity, Docker services, database migrations, and timeout utilities before starting\n- **Validates your PRD** — checks for missing test steps, vague requirements, and structural issues. If it finds problems, Claude auto-fixes them\n- **Verifies code after Claude writes it** — runs a 5-step pipeline: lint, unit tests, PRD test steps, API smoke test, frontend smoke test\n- **Learns from retries** — when a story fails then passes after retries, Ralph extracts what went wrong as a \"sign\" and remembers it for future stories (when `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config)\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Customize\n\nThese are things you run yourself to teach Ralph your preferences.\n\n### Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n### Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n### Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n> **Also automatic:** When `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config, Ralph extracts signs on its own from stories that fail then succeed after retries. You can review auto-extracted signs in `.ralph/signs.json`.\n\n---\n\n### Add Your Own PRD Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. This guide shows you how to teach Ralph your preferences so the code it writes feels like yours.\n\n---\n\n## What Happens Automatically\n\nThese features are set up and run for you — no manual steps needed.\n\n### Setup (`npx agentic-loop setup`)\n\nWhen you run setup, Ralph automatically:\n\n- **Detects your project type** (Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, fullstack) and creates `.ralph/config.json` with sensible defaults — test commands, URLs, directories\n- **Installs pre-commit hooks** that block secrets, hardcoded URLs, debug statements, and TODO/FIXME comments from being committed\n- **Installs Claude Code hooks** that warn in real-time while Claude is coding — catching secrets, hardcoded URLs, and debug statements before they're even saved\n- **Installs timeout utilities** on macOS (via `brew install coreutils`) so session time limits are enforced reliably\n\n### During the Loop (`npx agentic-loop run`)\n\nEach time Ralph starts or processes a story, it automatically:\n\n- **Runs preflight checks** — verifies API/frontend connectivity, Docker services, database migrations, and timeout utilities before starting\n- **Validates your PRD** — checks for missing test steps, vague requirements, and structural issues. If it finds problems, Claude auto-fixes them\n- **Verifies code after Claude writes it** — runs a 5-step pipeline: lint, unit tests, PRD test steps, API smoke test, frontend smoke test\n- **Learns from retries** — when a story fails then passes after retries, Ralph extracts what went wrong as a \"sign\" and remembers it for future stories (when `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config)\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Customize\n\nThese are things you run yourself to teach Ralph your preferences.\n\n### Tell Claude How You Like to Code\n\nRun `/my-dna` in a Claude session. Claude will ask you questions about how you like your code — naming style, how you handle errors, whether you prefer comments or self-documenting code. Your answers get saved and included in every Ralph session from that point on.\n\n```\n/my-dna\n```\n\n> **Tip:** You don't need to know the \"right\" answers. Just describe how you work. \"I like short functions\" or \"I always want error messages to be user-friendly\" is enough.\n\n---\n\n### Keep Your UI Consistent\n\nIf your project has a frontend, run `/styleguide` to generate a visual reference of your colors, typography, and component patterns. Ralph will use this as a reference when building new UI.\n\n```\n/styleguide\n```\n\nThis creates an HTML file you can open in your browser to see everything at a glance. Frontend stories reference it automatically.\n\n---\n\n### Teach Ralph From Its Mistakes\n\nWhen Ralph keeps making the same mistake — wrong import path, wrong naming convention, anything — you can teach it with `/sign`:\n\n```\n/sign \"Always use camelCase for API response fields\" backend\n```\n\n```\n/sign \"Import Button from @/components/ui, not shadcn directly\" frontend\n```\n\nThink of signs as sticky notes for Ralph. They get included in every prompt so it doesn't forget.\n\n> **Also automatic:** When `autoPromoteSigns` is enabled in config, Ralph extracts signs on its own from stories that fail then succeed after retries. You can review auto-extracted signs in `.ralph/signs.json`.\n\n---\n\n### Add Your Own PRD Rules\n\nEvery project has its own standards. You can add custom checks that run alongside the built-in ones. Just ask Claude:\n\n```\nCreate a prd-check that ensures every story has a description\n```\n\n```\nAdd a custom prd-check that warns if a story touches more than 10 files\n```\n\n```\nWrite a prd-check that requires backend stories to have error handling in their test steps\n```\n\nClaude will create the check script and put it in the right place (`.ralph/checks/prd/` inside your project). These checks run automatically every time Ralph validates a PRD.\n\n> **Good to know:** Built-in checks get auto-fixed by Claude when possible. Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you. See [Configuration Reference](RALPH.md#configuration-reference) for everything that's configurable.\n\n---\n\n### On-Demand Quality Checks\n\nThese aren't part of the automated loop — they're tools you can use whenever you want a second opinion:\n\n| Type this | What it does |\n|-----------|-------------|\n| `/vibe-check` | Scans for common AI coding patterns — leftover console.logs, TODOs, dead code |\n| `/review` | Full code review with suggestions for improvements |\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Feature | When it runs | Automatic or manual? |\n|---------|-------------|---------------------|\n| Project detection + config | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic |\n| Pre-commit hooks | Every `git commit` | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Claude Code hooks | While Claude edits files | Automatic (installed during setup) |\n| Timeout utility install | `npx agentic-loop setup` | Automatic (macOS with Homebrew) |\n| Preflight checks | Start of `npx agentic-loop run` | Automatic |\n| PRD validation + auto-fix | Start of loop | Automatic |\n| Code verification (5-step) | After Claude writes each story | Automatic |\n| Sign auto-promotion | After story retry succeeds | Automatic (if enabled) |\n| `/my-dna` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/styleguide` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/sign` | When you run it | Manual |\n| Custom PRD checks | When you create them | Manual (then runs automatically) |\n| `/vibe-check` | When you run it | Manual |\n| `/review` | When you run it | Manual |\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [Cheatsheet](CHEATSHEET.md) — All commands at a glance\n- [How Ralph Works](RALPH.md) — Full architecture\n- [Hooks Reference](HOOKS.md) — Details on the safety checks\n"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2681,"cache_read_input_tokens":55083,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2681},"output_tokens":24,"service_tier":"standard"}},"requestId":"req_011CXnMgJUAuGT4JWE9D6A1q","type":"assistant","uuid":"7138965b-4c88-4c67-8196-e28e4ad53396","timestamp":"2026-02-04T03:58:02.156Z"}

Custom checks get reported for you to review — Ralph won't try to guess what your custom rules mean.\n\nIf you want to temporarily turn off a custom check, ask Claude:\n\n```\nDisable the check-complexity prd-check\n```\n\n---\n\n### Tune Your Config\n\nIf you need to change how Ralph behaves — session length, retry limits, which URLs to test against — ask Claude:\n\n```\nSet Ralph's max session time to 10 minutes\n```\n\n```\nTurn off linting checks in Ralph\n```\n\nClaude will update `.ralph/config.json` for you.
